children.text: na jñānācchūnyatā nāma kācidanyā hi vidyate /
children.translated_text: There is no <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness) apart from knowledge;
for it is held that isolation is not different from that which is isolated. // 1 //

children.text: dvayaśūnyam hi vijñānam anyathā na prasajyate /
children.translated_text: <s>Vijñāna</s> (consciousness) is empty of the duality [of subject and object]; otherwise it would not be tenable,
because from the nonexistence of duality, that which has ceased would absurdly have the nature of duality. // 2 //
That which has the form of <s>tathatā</s> (suchness), thus heard, is declared to be the <s>Bhagavān</s> (Blessed One) himself,
who does not depend on the construction of the real existence of the knowable and the knower. // 3 //
<s>Cittamātra</s> (mind-only), free from appearances, abiding — this is the <s>Buddha-bhūmi</s> (Buddha-ground);
this indeed has been spoken by the <s>Buddhas</s>, they who shine and who cause to shine. // 4 //

children.text: cittaṃ hi bhūmayaḥ sapta nirābhāsā tvihāṣṭamī /
children.translated_text: The mind comprises seven <s>bhūmis</s> (stages); the eighth is free from appearances;
two stages constitute the abiding here; the remaining stage has the nature of 'mine'. // 5 //
Seven stages, governed by mind, are taught by the <s>Buddhas</s>;
on the seventh, the deficiency of body, speech, and mind no longer operates. // 6 //
On the eighth, its basis [is transformed]; even in dreams, unhappy conditions do not arise;
[lacuna] // 7
1. The <s>Dharma</s> that is inexpressible by words, yet was taught out of compassion —
homage to the <s>Buddha</s>, of inconceivable origin, whose awakening is unattached! // 8 //

children.text: 2. svabhāvena na cotpannā nirvṛtāśca na tattvataḥ /
children.translated_text: 2. Not arisen by their own nature, nor truly ceased,
like space, so are the <s>Buddhas</s>; and beings too have a single characteristic. // 9 //
3. Not arisen, neither from this shore nor from the far shore, born from conditions by their own nature —
those <s>saṃskāras</s> (formations) too are indeed empty, being the domain of omniscient wisdom. // 10 //
4. All phenomena are held to be like reflections by their own nature,
pure, of auspicious nature, nondual, and equal to <s>tathatā</s> (suchness). // 11 //
5. Ordinary beings, having imagined selfhood in what is without self,

children.text: sukhaduḥkham abhijñāśca sarvam eṣāṃ ca tattvataḥ // 12 //
children.translated_text: experience happiness and suffering — and all this is truly [experienced] by them. // 12 //
6. The six destinies of <s>saṃsāra</s> (cyclic existence), heavenly supreme happiness,
and great suffering in the hells, along with old age, disease, and also death. // 13 //
7. Having fabricated unreal imaginings, they are cooked in the hells and other realms;
they are burnt by their own faults alone, just as bamboo is consumed by its own fire. // 14 //

body.text: 8. yathā māyā tathā sattvā viṣayān paribhuñjate //
body.translated_text: 8. Just as an illusion, so do beings enjoy sense objects;
they go to illusory destinies, having the form of dependent origination. // 15 //

children.translated_text: 9. Just as a painter, having drawn the terrifying form of a <s>yakṣa</s>,
is himself frightened by it — so is the ignorant one in <s>saṃsāra</s>. // 16 //

children.text: 10. yathā paṅkaṃ svayaṃ kṛtvā kaścit patati bāliśaḥ /
children.translated_text: 10. Just as a foolish person, having created mud himself, falls into it,
so beings are sunk in the mud of unreal imagination, which is hard to cross. // 17 //

children.text: 11. abhāvaṃ bhavato dṛṣṭvā duḥkhāṃ vindati vedanām /
children.translated_text: 11. Seeing existence from nonexistence, one experiences painful sensation;
just so, unreal sense objects afflict, like poison born of suspicion. // 18 //
12. Seeing those beings who are without refuge, with minds firm in compassion,
the <s>Buddhas</s>, who are benefactors, direct beings toward <s>sambodhi</s> (complete awakening). // 19 //
13. They too, having accumulated the provisions [of merit and wisdom], attaining unsurpassed knowledge,
freed from the net of conceptual construction, become <s>Buddhas</s>, kinsmen of the world. // 20 //
14. Since the unborn is unarisen, those who correctly see the welfare of beings,
seeing the world as empty, devoid of beginning, middle, and end — // 21 //

children.text: 15. tena paśyanti saṃsāraṃ nirvāṇaṃ ca na cātmanaḥ /
children.translated_text: 15. Therefore they see <s>saṃsāra</s> and <s>nirvāṇa</s> as not [belonging to] a self,
unstained, unchanging, and luminous in the beginning, middle, and end. // 22 //
16. One who has awakened does not see the objects experienced in a dream;
likewise, one awakened from the sleep of delusion does not see <s>saṃsāra</s>. // 23 //
17. When a magician, having created an illusion, withdraws it,

children.text: tadā na vidyate kiṃcid dharmāṇāṃ sā hi dharmatā // 24 //
children.translated_text: then nothing whatsoever exists — such indeed is the <s>dharmatā</s> (true nature) of all <s>dharmas</s>. // 24 //
18. All this is <s>cittamātra</s> (mind-only), arisen like the work of a magician;

children.text: tataḥ śubhāśubhaṃ karma tato janma śubhāśubham // 25 //
children.translated_text: from that arises wholesome and unwholesome <s>karma</s>, and from that, fortunate and unfortunate birth. // 25 //

children.text: 19. kalpayanti yathā lokaṃ notpannāśca svayaṃ janāḥ /
children.translated_text: 19. Just as people imagine the world, yet they themselves have not arisen,

children.text: utpādo hi vikalpo 'yaṃ artho bāhyo na vidyate // 26 //
children.translated_text: for this arising is mere conceptual construction — no external object exists. // 26 //
20. In phenomena that are without own-nature, those who perceive permanence, self, and happiness,
the foolish, covered by the darkness of delusion, wander in this ocean of existence. // 27 //
Of this great ocean of <s>saṃsāra</s>, filled with the waters of conceptual construction,

children.text: anākramya mahāyānaṃ ko vā pāraṃ tariṣyati // 28 //
children.translated_text: without boarding the <s>Mahāyāna</s> (Great Vehicle), who indeed will cross to the other shore? // 28 //

body.translated_text: The <s>Mahāyānaviṃśikā</s> (Twenty Verses on the Mahāyāna), composed by the noble <s>Nāgārjuna</s>.
